newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - NYH diffs up on MTBE, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - NYH diffs up on MTBE, trade quiet.

text.p: U.S. cash products differentials were mostly steady amid a complex-wide quiet day of trade on Thursday, although New York Harbor gasoline showed some gains on the strength of MTBE.
NYMEX crude oil and product futures, meanwhile, were treading water in the middle of the session's range as players await the flood of Iraqi oil, expected in August.
August gasoline was up 0.78 cents at 61.90 cents a gallon, while heating oil was up 0.12 at 53.40 cents.
NEW YORK HARBOR
The recent rally of key gasoline blending component MTBE was firming prices of reformulated and high octane gasoline grades, dealers said.

"The prices are all MTBE related, and we will probably see relatively firm levels through the middle of next month," said a dealer who noted gasoline imports also were decreasing due to a less attractive arbitrage from Europe.

The reformulated gaosline A2-grade was done at 2.25 over NYMEX after being offered at 1.90 over earlier in the week. High octane 93-grade was offered at 11.75 over the NYMEX and was seen lean towards 12.00 cents over.
Conventional unleaded was offered at four cents under, in line with late yesterday.
U.S. GULF
Activity was quiet in the U.S. Gulf Coast. A customer outing sponsored by BP Oil in Cleveland, Ohio, took many players out of their offices for the day.

On the gasoline side, differentials for the front 22nd cycle of conventional M1-grade gasoline, now the prompt, were at 2.00 cent to 2.25 cents below September futures. Any month barrels were talked 3.25/3.00 cent below the screen.
The back 21st cycle on the Colonial Pipeline, the main artery from the Gulf to the East Coast, reached a scheduling deadling late Wednesday.
"It's very quiet. The only news people are talking is the BP outing," said a Gulf trader.
Prompt reformulated A1-grade gasoline remained steady at even to about 25 cent over September NYMEX futures.
The distillates were mostly steady, with an August paper deal done at 0.30 cent over the print for 54-grade jet fuel.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent markets were quiet Thursday morning, with prompt cash differentials remaining steady at higher levels reached yesterday on hype of refinery trouble.

In Group Three hub, prompt unleaded gasoline differentials held at 0.50/0.75 cents over August NYMEX, after gaining a half cent Wednesday. The pop was due to a partial shutdown of the gasoline making unit of National Cooperative Refinery Association's McPherson, Kansas, plant.
Chicago material also stayed stable at 0.75/1.00 cent over the print, with any months on par.
"It's fairly quiet all around. It's just the tone of the market," said a Group player.
The distillates were also quiet, and hovering at yesterday's higher levels. Group low sulphur diesel was 2.25/2.50 cents over August NYMEX and Chicago was 0.50/0.25 cents below the screen.
--New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
